body.p: . Fills COMPLEX_TYPES and the content model plan of (src/schema_complex_type.c, src/schema_content_model.c).

item.p: One automaton format. A content model is states whose transitions are labelled by an element declaration (with the declarations substitutable for it, 3.3.6.3) or a schema wildcard and carry counter tests (a counter in a range) and counter operations (set to one, add one); final states may need tests. Sequences and choices compile through Glushkov's position automaton and a subset construction; an all group compiles to two states (before and after the first member) whose transitions count each member. The matcher, list_expected and the restriction walk step this one format.

Expansion, counters, determinism. A particle with maxOccurs (or, unbounded, minOccurs) up to 16 is expanded into copies, a larger one keeps one copy under a counter; a compilation past the state limit is tried again counting every repetition above one. When the counters cannot choose between two transitions of one particle ((a{1,20}){1,20}, (a+){1,100}: weakly but not strongly deterministic) the counted particles involved are expanded and the model compiled again, so the matcher never backtracks and needs one state and one value per counter. When that expansion passes the limit too (MS particlesZ035, Z036, maxOccurs in the thousands nested), the counters are kept and the transitions ordered (fewer operations first, so an inner repetition before an outer one); the matcher takes the first whose tests hold, exact unless an outer minimum needs the inner repetitions spread. Bounds: the configured states (and positions), 4 nodes, 32 edges or transitions and 64 list entries per state.

UPA as determinism (cos-nonambig): two transitions of a state for different element particles sharing a name (also through substitution groups), or for different wildcard particles whose namespaces overlap, whose tests can hold together. An element particle beats a wildcard particle (3.8.6.4). Exclusive counter tests do not compete: (a{2}, a) is valid.

Substitution groups: a head's transition lists the head and each member substitutable for it (blocking by the head's disallowed substitutions, its type's and the intermediate types' prohibited substitutions). Abstract declarations are listed too ( said not): the validator raises cvc-elt.2 for them, as for an abstract head.
Open content is the matcher's fallback; suffix mode appends a suffix state that only its wildcard enters and keeps.

Restriction of content (cos-content-act-restrict, 3.4.6.4) is a walk over pairs of configurations (state and counter values) of the two models: each move of the restriction, element by element (and each name a restriction's wildcard shares with the base's element transitions), must be a move of the base whose default binding subsumes the restriction's; names the restriction takes by an element are not its wildcard's. A base wildcard with no global declaration of the name takes the restriction's local element whatever its process contents (XSD 1.0's NSCompat; read literally 3.4.6.4 refuses it, against the suite: MS particlesJ, ctG). Past 65,536 configurations the derivation is accepted provisionally, as 3.4.6.3 allows.

The stage: particles (p-props-correct), attribute groups (closures over cyclic references, 3.6.2.1, then written), complex types base first with an explicit stack (content type of 3.4.2.2 and 3.4.2.3.3 with the synthesized particles, simple content types through sxml_schema_compile_simple_type, attribute uses and wildcards with wildcard union and intersection, assertions; cos-ct-extends, derivation-ok-restriction, ct-props-correct; the content model; registration), xs:anyType's and xs:untyped's content models, then element declarations (e-props-correct 2, 4, 6, 7; value constraints cast to the simple type). Attribute restriction is checked with XSD 1.0's clauses (uses allowed, types derived, fixed values, required kept, wildcard subset, not weaker), not against xs:anyType.
Registration: a complex type with a simple base is registered with base xs:anyType, since sxml_type_registry_register_schema_type takes only complex bases for complex types (Proposed).
Text form: sxml_schema_content_model_write_text prints a model in 's form, for 5.4's sxml_schema_components_write_text.

Not done: type table equivalence (cos-element-consistent clause 4 and the wildcard clause), the disallowed-names clauses of Wildcard Subset, cos-ct-extends 1.5 and 1.6 and derivation-ok-restriction.4 (locally declared types), xs:assertion facets of simpleContent restrictions.

Measured (schema tests only, with 5.4's uncommitted reader; the instance tests wait for 5.7): MS-Particles 851 of 853 run, ModelGroups 377 of 391, Group 215 of 218, ComplexType 546 of 550, Wildcards 313 of 315, Sun MGroup 40 of 40, CType 31 of 31, Saxon All 62 of 62, Open 49 of 51, IBM allGroup 9 of 9, openContent 24 of 24. The rest are the reader's (duplicate ids, an all group with maxOccurs 0 accepted by XSD 1.1, openContent mode="none" with a wildcard, xs:redefine of a group) or disputed by the versions (particlesK006).
